questions.stem: Why are proteins only used as a respiratory substrate as a last resort, such as during starvation?

options.text: Proteins are too large to enter the mitochondria
Proteins release less energy than carbohydrates
Proteins have essential functions in the body and their breakdown produces toxic ammonia
Proteins cannot be broken down by enzymes

questions.explanation: Proteins serve vital structural and functional roles in the body (enzymes, antibodies, muscle). Breaking them down for energy also produces ammonia, which is toxic and must be converted to urea in the liver.
